reasons_add: ITQAN (Ubayy b. Kaʿb) reports that neither Torah nor Gospel contains the like of the Mother of the Qur'an, the seven oft-repeated verses. ITQAN (ʿAbd Allāh b. Jābir) calls the opening praise the Qur'an's best surah; ITQAN (Anas) calls it the best of the Qur'an; ITQAN (Abū Saʿīd b. al-Muʿallā) calls it the greatest surah.
ITQAN (Ubayy b. Kaʿb) calls it the Mother of the Qur'an and reports that neither Torah nor Gospel contains its like.
ITQAN (Ubayy b. Kaʿb) identifies the Mother of the Qur'an as the seven oft-repeated verses and says the earlier scriptures contain nothing like it.

ITQAN (author) reports an explanation of the move from third-person praise to direct-address worship: worship ranks above praise, and the move observes etiquette toward God. ITQAN (Ibn ʿAbbās) reports that the Opening of the Book equals two-thirds of the Qur'an.
ITQAN (author) reports an alternative explanation that praise uses the third person and worship direct address because worship ranks above praise; the shift also observes etiquette toward God.
